intended_object: The canonical E-linear inclusion of the degree-j graded piece A_j of an algebra R graded by `NatOrdinal` into its finite-degree part A_{<ω} (the subalgebra spanned by the pieces of finite degree). Inferred from the docstring and from how the module uses it.
explanation: The map sends a ∈ 𝒜 j to the same element of R, now seen as an element of `finiteDegreePart 𝒜`. Membership comes from `mem_finiteDegreePart_of_mem`. Additivity and scalar compatibility hold by `rfl`. This is exactly the inclusion A_j ↪ A_{<ω}. It is a special case of Mathlib's `Submodule.inclusion` (applied to 𝒜 j ≤ (finiteDegreePart 𝒜).toSubmodule). Writing it out directly is a convenience whose codomain is the subalgebra type. It does not add any restriction on generality. The setting (field E, NatOrdinal grading) is the library's own setting for finite-degree parts, and the inclusion uses nothing beyond it. Nothing degenerate goes wrong.
